subtitle: Bridge of Sighs, 1831. Henry Hutchinson built it. You will not.
restart: Click, tap or Space to rebuild and go again
intro: Drag, move the mouse or use Left/Right to punt. Click, tap or Space to launch
facts: The Bridge of Sighs was built in 1831 to a design by Henry Hutchinson.
It links Third Court to New Court across the Cam.
It is a Grade I listed building. Please stop hitting it.
It is named after the Bridge of Sighs in Venice, which it does not much resemble.
College punts run from the start of Easter Term to the end of October.
Book College punts from the Cripps Porters' Lodge: GBP8 an hour.
PuntSoc volunteers who help look after the punts punt for free.
Grad sports teams can apply for funding to replace balls, clubs and other kit.
SBR tournaments and casual sport run all year. Everyone is welcome.
The Samuel Butler Room was founded in 1960.
Samuel Butler studied at St John's from 1854 to 1858.
The SBR room is at I2, First Court.
BA Table: Tuesdays and Fridays in term.
Port & Sherry: Fridays after hall, GBP1.50.
splashes: Into the Cam. The tourists applaud.

overs: The Domestic Bursar would like a word about the bridge.

clears: Bridge demolished. New Court is now an island.

The College is rebuilding it. Faster this time.
